children.text: A nucleus with \(Z\) protons, \(N\) neutrons and \(A=Z+N\) has rest energy \(mc^2=Am_Nc^2-B\). Use the model \[B=a_VA-a_SA^{2/3}-a_CZ^2/A^{1/3}-a_{sym}(N-Z)^2/A,\] where \(a_V=15.8\), \(a_S=17.8\), \(a_C=0.711\), \(a_{sym}=23.7\), all in MeV. Ignore omitted corrections and proton-neutron mass differences.
Under \(Z=N\), find the mass number maximizing \(B/A\).
For fixed \(A=197\), maximize binding over \(Z\) to find \(Z^*\).
Equal fission is favourable if \(m(Z,N)>2m(Z/2,N/2)\). Express this as \(Z^2/A>C_{fission}a_S/a_C\) and find the coefficient to two significant figures.

For a large neutron-only nucleus, \(M=m_NA\), \(R=R_0A^{1/3}\), with \(R_0=1.1\,\mathrm{fm}\). Add binding \(B_{grav}=3GM^2/(5R)=a_{grav}A^{5/3}\). Find \(a_{grav}\) in MeV and the threshold \(A_c\) for positive total binding, ignoring the surface term. Use \(m_Nc^2=939\,\mathrm{MeV}\), \(G=\hbar c/M_P^2\), \(M_Pc^2=1.22\times10^{22}\,\mathrm{MeV}\), \(\hbar c=197\,\mathrm{MeV\,fm}\). Give one significant figure.

Clock I is a height \(\Delta h>0\) above clock II in constant downward gravity \(g\). A free-falling reference F starts at rest at I. Use \(\Delta\phi=g\Delta h\), \(v^2=2\Delta\phi\), and the source's first-order clock comparison to express lower-clock interval \(\Delta\tau_{II}\) in terms of \(\Delta\tau_I\).

Find leading excess travel time for \(d\ll|x_N|,x_E\) and \(GM_{WD}\ll c^2d\).

In a circular neutron-star binary, write \(\omega=\chi R^p\), with \(\chi\) independent of \(R,\omega\). Find \(p\) ignoring relativity.

statement.text:
Neutron Stars
A nucleus with \(Z\) protons, \(N\) neutrons and \(A=Z+N\) has rest energy \(mc^2=Am_Nc^2-B\). Use the model \[B=a_VA-a_SA^{2/3}-a_CZ^2/A^{1/3}-a_{sym}(N-Z)^2/A,\] where \(a_V=15.8\), \(a_S=17.8\), \(a_C=0.711\), \(a_{sym}=23.7\), all in MeV. Ignore omitted corrections and proton-neutron mass differences.
A.1. Largest binding per nucleon
Under \(Z=N\), find the mass number maximizing \(B/A\).
A.2. Stable atomic number
For fixed \(A=197\), maximize binding over \(Z\) to find \(Z^*\).
A.3. Equal-fission threshold
Equal fission is favourable if \(m(Z,N)>2m(Z/2,N/2)\). Express this as \(Z^2/A>C_{fission}a_S/a_C\) and find the coefficient to two significant figures.
B.1. Gravitational binding threshold
For a large neutron-only nucleus, \(M=m_NA\), \(R=R_0A^{1/3}\), with \(R_0=1.1\,\mathrm{fm}\). Add binding \(B_{grav}=3GM^2/(5R)=a_{grav}A^{5/3}\). Find \(a_{grav}\) in MeV and the threshold \(A_c\) for positive total binding, ignoring the surface term. Use \(m_Nc^2=939\,\mathrm{MeV}\), \(G=\hbar c/M_P^2\), \(M_Pc^2=1.22\times10^{22}\,\mathrm{MeV}\), \(\hbar c=197\,\mathrm{MeV\,fm}\). Give one significant figure.
C.1. Gravitational clock rate
Clock I is a height \(\Delta h>0\) above clock II in constant downward gravity \(g\). A free-falling reference F starts at rest at I. Use \(\Delta\phi=g\Delta h\), \(v^2=2\Delta\phi\), and the source's first-order clock comparison to express lower-clock interval \(\Delta\tau_{II}\) in terms of \(\Delta\tau_I\).
C.2. Shapiro time delay

A neutron star N at \(x_N<0\) emits light towards Earth E at \(x_E>0\). A white dwarf of mass \(M_{WD}\) is at perpendicular distance \(d\) from the straight light path, closest at \(x=0\). Take \(\phi(\infty)=0\) and \(c_{eff}\simeq(1+2\phi/c^2)c\). Find leading excess travel time for \(d\ll|x_N|,x_E\) and \(GM_{WD}\ll c^2d\).
C.3. Binary delay range

N and W orbit circularly at separation \(L\), with a small angle \(\varepsilon\) between orbital plane and line to Earth. Find maximum minus minimum white-dwarf delay. The extremes have \(x_N\simeq-L\) and \(x_N\simeq L\). Other gravitational delays cancel.
C.4. White-dwarf mass from data

The original delay graph is for \(L\simeq6\times10^6\,\mathrm{km}\), \(\cos\varepsilon\simeq0.99989\). Read its delay range and find \(M_{WD}/M_\odot\) to one significant figure. Use \(GM_\odot/c^3\simeq5\,\mathrm{\mu s}\).
C.5. Inspiral frequency exponent
In a circular neutron-star binary, write \(\omega=\chi R^p\), with \(\chi\) independent of \(R,\omega\). Find \(p\) ignoring relativity.
C.6. Gravitational-wave profile

Wave amplitude is proportional to \(R^2\omega^2\). Select the most appropriate of the four original profiles before collision.

children.text: Here \(B/A=a_V-a_SA^{-1/3}-a_CA^{2/3}/4\). Set the derivative to zero to get \(A=2a_S/a_C\simeq50\).

Volume and symmetry terms cancel. Surface cost competes with Coulomb release, giving \[C_{fission}=\frac{2^{1/3}-1}{1-2^{-2/3}}=0.70.\] This is an energy criterion and does not remove a fission barrier.

\[a_{grav}=\frac{3Gm_N^2}{5R_0}=6.4\times10^{-37}\,\mathrm{MeV}\simeq6\times10^{-37}\,\mathrm{MeV}.\] Positive binding requires \((a_V-a_{sym})A+a_{grav}A^{5/3}>0\), so \[A_c=[(a_{sym}-a_V)/a_{grav}]^{3/2}=4.4\times10^{55}\simeq4\times10^{55}.\] This is the source's positive-total-binding criterion, an estimate rather than a complete neutron-star stability calculation.

The lower clock runs more slowly. To first order, \[\Delta\tau_{II}=(1-\Delta\phi/c^2)\Delta\tau_I.\] The given local falling-frame argument uses \(\sqrt{1-v^2/c^2}\simeq1-v^2/(2c^2)\). The intervals refer to the source's comparison, not an assertion that an accelerated stationary clock is globally inertial.

At the maximum, \(d\simeq L\varepsilon\), giving \(\Delta t_{max}=(2GM_{WD}/c^3)\ln[4x_E/(L\varepsilon^2)]\). At the minimum N is in front of W, so the same integral has positive lower limit and gives \(\Delta t_{min}=(2GM_{WD}/c^3)\ln(x_E/L)\). Therefore \[\Delta t_{max}-\Delta t_{min}=\frac{2GM_{WD}}{c^3}\ln(4/\varepsilon^2).\]
The graph range is about \(50\,\mathrm{\mu s}\), and \(\varepsilon^2\simeq2(1-\cos\varepsilon)=0.00022\). Thus \(M_{WD}/M_\odot=50/[10\ln(4/0.00022)]\simeq0.5\).
Radiation makes binding energy more negative, so \(R\) decreases. Frequency grows as \(R^{-3/2}\), and amplitude grows as \(R^{-1}\). Choose profile (b), with increasing amplitude and frequency.

solution.text:
Neutron Stars
A.1. Largest binding per nucleon
Here \(B/A=a_V-a_SA^{-1/3}-a_CA^{2/3}/4\). Set the derivative to zero to get \(A=2a_S/a_C\simeq50\).
A.2. Stable atomic number
\(\partial B/\partial Z=0\) yields \[Z^*=\frac{A}{2[1+a_CA^{2/3}/(4a_{sym})]}\simeq79.\]
A.3. Equal-fission threshold
Volume and symmetry terms cancel. Surface cost competes with Coulomb release, giving \[C_{fission}=\frac{2^{1/3}-1}{1-2^{-2/3}}=0.70.\] This is an energy criterion and does not remove a fission barrier.
B.1. Gravitational binding threshold
\[a_{grav}=\frac{3Gm_N^2}{5R_0}=6.4\times10^{-37}\,\mathrm{MeV}\simeq6\times10^{-37}\,\mathrm{MeV}.\] Positive binding requires \((a_V-a_{sym})A+a_{grav}A^{5/3}>0\), so \[A_c=[(a_{sym}-a_V)/a_{grav}]^{3/2}=4.4\times10^{55}\simeq4\times10^{55}.\] This is the source's positive-total-binding criterion, an estimate rather than a complete neutron-star stability calculation.
C.1. Gravitational clock rate
The lower clock runs more slowly. To first order, \[\Delta\tau_{II}=(1-\Delta\phi/c^2)\Delta\tau_I.\] The given local falling-frame argument uses \(\sqrt{1-v^2/c^2}\simeq1-v^2/(2c^2)\). The intervals refer to the source's comparison, not an assertion that an accelerated stationary clock is globally inertial.
C.2. Shapiro time delay
Expand reciprocal speed and integrate \(\phi=-GM_{WD}/\sqrt{x^2+d^2}\): \[\Delta t=\frac{2GM_{WD}}{c^3}\int_{x_N}^{x_E}\frac{dx}{\sqrt{x^2+d^2}}\simeq\frac{2GM_{WD}}{c^3}\ln\frac{4|x_N|x_E}{d^2}.\]
C.3. Binary delay range
At the maximum, \(d\simeq L\varepsilon\), giving \(\Delta t_{max}=(2GM_{WD}/c^3)\ln[4x_E/(L\varepsilon^2)]\). At the minimum N is in front of W, so the same integral has positive lower limit and gives \(\Delta t_{min}=(2GM_{WD}/c^3)\ln(x_E/L)\). Therefore \[\Delta t_{max}-\Delta t_{min}=\frac{2GM_{WD}}{c^3}\ln(4/\varepsilon^2).\]
C.4. White-dwarf mass from data
The graph range is about \(50\,\mathrm{\mu s}\), and \(\varepsilon^2\simeq2(1-\cos\varepsilon)=0.00022\). Thus \(M_{WD}/M_\odot=50/[10\ln(4/0.00022)]\simeq0.5\).
C.5. Inspiral frequency exponent
Kepler's law gives \(\omega^2R^3=\mathrm{constant}\), so \(p=-3/2\).
C.6. Gravitational-wave profile
Radiation makes binding energy more negative, so \(R\) decreases. Frequency grows as \(R^{-3/2}\), and amplitude grows as \(R^{-1}\). Choose profile (b), with increasing amplitude and frequency.
